Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed head-on motor vehicle collision with complaints of neck and low back pain.
The reported mechanism is consistent with the injuries described, and the patient has no known prior injury to the
cervical or lumbar regions. Over the course of nine visits, care consisted of spinal mobilization, soft tissue therapy,
home stretching instruction, and graded activity. The treatment followed a typical course, with visit frequency reduced
as symptoms improved and the patient was discharged to self-directed exercise. Most of the clinical picture rests on
the patient's own pain reports, as cervical and lumbar range of motion, neurological screening, and orthopedic
provocation tests were unremarkable, and cervical and lumbar imaging obtained at intake showed no acute
abnormality. Two similar treatment charges recorded on the same date of service are under review for billing
accuracy. Prognosis is good with continued home exercise.
